item.revised_prompt: The X-shaped geometric layout of four diagonal blue lines intersecting at the center and terminating in four red circular points in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The target image shows a compact quadcopter for everyday aerial photography in a strict orthographic top view on a plain light background, omitting the black background and guide marks of <Picture 1> while aligning its unfolded arms and motor centers with <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> supplies the exact spatial positions of the four motor centers, equal horizontal and vertical spacing, and diagonal arm directions transferred to the quadcopter's frame. The quadcopter features a true X-frame configuration with a 250 mm opposite-motor span, oriented with its nose pointing toward the top edge of the canvas. At the center is a box-shaped fuselage shell with straight sides, clipped corners, and a plain, seamless top cover, finished in a uniform matte light grey that extends continuously into the four fully unfolded arms. Each arm emerges from the central shell through a smooth, seamless blend without any joint line at the root. At the front tip, the nose shell wraps smoothly around a horizontally forward-facing camera so that only the sleek top surface of the nose is visible from overhead, with no gimbal arms or side lugs protruding. Positioned precisely at the four terminal points of <Subject 1>, each dark grey cylindrical motor mounts a single stationary, guardless two-blade black propeller with five-inch blades resting flat against the light background.
